biggest_catch: The $95 annual fee plus the temptation to overspend to hit $5,000 in 3 months. Year-one math: 75,000 points are worth at least $750 as cash back through Chase Ultimate Rewards, so $750 bonus value minus the $95 fee leaves roughly $655 net in the first year. Only claim this if you were already going to spend that $5,000 on normal purchases; never spend extra just to hit the target. Also, Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern means you can be denied if you've opened five or more personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months, and a new Sapphire bonus is unavailable if you've earned one in the past 48 months or currently hold a Sapphire card.
catches: Only claim this if you were already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $5,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: the 75,000-point bonus is worth at least $750 as cash back, minus the $95 annual fee, which leaves about $655 net in year one. From year two the $95 fee applies without any bonus, so only keep the card if the rewards you earn from normal spending beat that $95.

Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry, which typically knocks a few points off your credit score for a short time. Chase also uses its unpublished 5/24 pattern: applicants with five or more newly opened personal cards across any issuer in the last 24 months are generally denied.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.

Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even with excellent credit. This is not published in Chase's official terms, so confirm your own history first.

A new Sapphire bonus is not available if you received a Sapphire bonus in the past 48 months or currently hold a Sapphire card. If you fall inside that window, apply only after checking the current application terms.
The account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid, and the bonus is paid only once per account. Miss a payment around the time the bonus posts and you can lose it.

steps: Go to the official Chase Sapphire Preferred page and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm your eligibility: you have not received a Sapphire new-cardmember bonus in the last 48 months and do not currently hold a Sapphire card.
Apply online. Expect a hard credit inquiry.
Use the card for the purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $5,000 in the first 3 months from account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the 75,000 points to post, and confirm they appear in your Ultimate Rewards account.
Before the second $95 annual fee hits, decide whether to keep the card or downgrade to a no-fee Chase card based on what the card earns you in normal use.
